name: Snap-on smile
lead: Snap-On Smile is a removable cosmetic dental appliance made by the dental company DenMat. It is a thin tooth-borne overdenture that fits over a person's existing teeth, and it changes the look of the smile at once: shade, shape and apparent alignment are replaced by those of the appliance, without drilling or bonding [1][2][7]. It is described in the dental literature as a temporary esthetic option rather than a permanent restoration [3]. In appearance culture, the term is also used generically for removable "fake veneers" that snap over the natural teeth.

Dentists have written about it mainly in case reports: for older patients with failing dentition and jaw disease, for people with the hereditary enamel disorder amelogenesis imperfecta, and as a provisional restoration during implant treatment [3][4][5][6]. These publications are clinician-authored case descriptions and do not include controlled trials.

paras: The appliance is described as a tooth-borne overdenture used for several temporary esthetic purposes [7]. One dental report describes a Snap-On Smile appliance fabricated from crystallized acetyl resin, and notes that the benefit can be limited in patients with a high smile line or altered gum architecture because the teeth can look too large; the author describes adding gum-colored silicone chairside to recreate gingival anatomy [7].

A 2013 article presented the appliance as a convenient solution for geriatric patients [3]. A 2016 report followed a 78-year-old man with osteonecrosis of the jaw and mandibular surgery, for whom most standard dental procedures were contraindicated, and described the appliance as restoring speech, chewing function and appearance over five years [1].

A 2015 paper discussed its use alongside facial esthetics for patients with amelogenesis imperfecta, a hereditary enamel disorder in which teeth can be discolored, sensitive and prone to decay, and in which patients often face psychosocial effects from appearance [2]. Other articles describe a quadrant version used as an implant temporary and further clinical applications [4][5][6][8].

A 2020 article describes indirect snap-on provisional restorations for porcelain veneer cases, in analog and digital workflows; the authors say such provisionals are easier for patients to keep clean, which supports healthier gums before final cementation, and report that patients seem to accept the approach [10]. In that use the snap-on shell is a stand-in that lets a patient wear and judge a new smile before permanent veneers are bonded [10][9].

One report notes that the appliance's benefit can be limited in patients with high smile lines or altered gum architecture because the teeth can look too large, and describes recreating gum anatomy with silicone on an acetal resin appliance [7]. Reports describe the product as temporary and removable, so it differs from bonded porcelain or composite veneers, which are made for long-term wear and require enamel preparation [9].

No controlled trials were found. The published literature consists of clinician case reports and case series, including a five-year follow-up of a single patient [1][2][4][5][6][8][10]. These describe feasibility and patient acceptance in individual cases, and the five-year report followed a 78-year-old man with osteonecrosis of the jaw, mandibular resection and rampant caries [1].

Removable snap-on veneers are discussed in appearance communities as a non-invasive alternative to permanent veneers, which involve tooth preparation [9]. The dental literature on the branded product concerns medical and provisional uses rather than cosmetic purchases by people with healthy teeth.

card.summary: A removable snap-over smile appliance from DenMat; documented in dental case reports as a temporary fix, with no trials behind it.
card.note: Evidence is case reports only; designed as a provisional appliance.

quick.overview:
Snap-On Smile is a thin removable appliance that fits over the existing teeth to change how the smile looks. It is a branded dental product, and the term is also used loosely online for removable fake veneers.

The published literature is made up of dentists' case reports, mostly on older or medically complex patients, enamel disorders and implant provisionals.
quick.mechanism: The appliance is a tooth-borne overdenture, reported to be made from acetal resin, that covers the teeth without altering them.
quick.risks: No trials have assessed it. Reports note the teeth can look too large in people with high smile lines or altered gums. It is described as temporary.

chain: A thin removable shell is made to fit over the existing teeth
Snaps on without altering the teeth
Shade, shape and spacing of the visible smile change
angle.text: The appliance gives a new-looking smile immediately and can be taken out. Dentists have described it for temporary use in medical cases, enamel disorders and as a trial or provisional before permanent work.
